memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If anyone borrows an animal from their neighbor and it is injured or dies while the owner is not present, they must make restitution. But if the owner is with the animal, the borrower will not have to pay. If the animal was hired, the money paid for the hire covers the loss." - Exodus 22:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's law now turns to the simple, everyday matter of borrowing. If you borrow something and it is harmed while in your care, you make it right. This is basic neighbourliness — treating what belongs to another with the same care you would give your own, and taking responsibility if it is damaged in your hands.

There is real godliness in these small, ordinary faithfulnesses. How we handle a borrowed tool, a lent book, a friend's car, or a returned favour reveals the quality of our character. It is easy to be careless with what is not ours, to return things late or damaged with a shrug. But God's people are called to treat others' belongings — and others' trust — as something precious. Faithfulness in little things is the soil where genuine integrity grows.

Jesus taught that whoever is faithful with very little will be faithful with much (Luke 16:10). Our God notices the small stewardships. And in a beautiful way, this reflects His own heart, for He handles what is entrusted to Him with perfect faithfulness — including us. He guards what belongs to Him and never treats His own carelessly. As we care well for what we borrow, we quietly reflect the faithful God who cares perfectly for us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I treat borrowed things and others' trust with genuine care?
Where might I have been careless with what does not belong to me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are faithful with all that is entrusted to You, including me. Make me trustworthy in small things, caring well for what others place in my hands. Amen.
